task.prompt:
In Arcady's garden there grows a peculiar apple-tree that fruits one time per year. Its peculiarity can be explained in following way: there are n inflorescences, numbered from 1 to n. Inflorescence number 1 is situated near base of tree and any other inflorescence with number i (i > 1) is situated at the top of branch, which bottom is p_{i}-th inflorescence and p_{i} < i.

Once tree starts fruiting, there appears exactly one apple in each inflorescence. The same moment as apples appear, they start to roll down along branches to the very base of tree. Each second all apples, except ones in first inflorescence simultaneously roll down one branch closer to tree base, e.g. apple in a-th inflorescence gets to p_{a}-th inflorescence. Apples that end up in first inflorescence are gathered by Arcady in exactly the same moment. Second peculiarity of this tree is that once two apples are in same inflorescence they annihilate. This happens with each pair of apples, e.g. if there are 5 apples in same inflorescence in same time, only one will not be annihilated and if there are 8 apples, all apples will be annihilated. Thus, there can be no more than one apple in each inflorescence in each moment of time.

Help Arcady with counting number of apples he will be able to collect from first inflorescence during one harvest.


-----Input-----

First line of input contains single integer number n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100 000)  — number of inflorescences.

Second line of input contains sequence of n - 1 integer numbers p_2, p_3, ..., p_{n} (1 ≤ p_{i} < i), where p_{i} is number of inflorescence into which the apple from i-th inflorescence rolls down.


-----Output-----

Single line of output should contain one integer number: amount of apples that Arcady will be able to collect from first inflorescence during one harvest.


-----Examples-----
Input
3
1 1

Output
1

Input
5
1 2 2 2

Output
3

Input
18
1 1 1 4 4 3 2 2 2 10 8 9 9 9 10 10 4

Output
4



-----Note-----

In first example Arcady will be able to collect only one apple, initially situated in 1st inflorescence. In next second apples from 2nd and 3rd inflorescences will roll down and annihilate, and Arcady won't be able to collect them.

In the second example Arcady will be able to collect 3 apples. First one is one initially situated in first inflorescence. In a second apple from 2nd inflorescence will roll down to 1st (Arcady will collect it) and apples from 3rd, 4th, 5th inflorescences will roll down to 2nd. Two of them will annihilate and one not annihilated will roll down from 2-nd inflorescence to 1st one in the next second and Arcady will collect it.

response.applicability: Apply when `task_public.prompt` clearly describes the rooted apple-tree / inflorescence problem with pairwise annihilation, `task_public.function_name` is empty (stdio task), and the submitted `candidate_code` appears unfinished or malformed in a live execution path: empty source, AST parse failure, `pass` statements, `TODO`/`NotImplemented` markers, or self-debugging commentary such as 'this is wrong' / 'confusing'. The repair replaces the incomplete submission with a complete deterministic solver using the invariant that the root receives an apple at time `t` iff the number of nodes at depth `t` is odd, so the answer is the count of depths with odd population. Runs in O(n) time and O(n) memory for up to 100000 nodes. Declines on non-matching prompts or non-stdio tasks.
response.description:
This operator performs a guarded code-repair rewrite for a narrow failure pattern: incomplete generated submissions on the apple-tree annihilation task. It first checks that the task prompt matches the specific rooted-tree story and that the task is stdio-based. It then detects unfinished implementation signals in `candidate_code` using static evidence: empty source, parse failure, live `pass`, TODO/NotImplemented text, or deliberative comments typical of abandoned generation. When both conditions hold, it replaces the candidate with a complete solver.

The synthesized solver uses the key algebraic invariant for the task: after pairwise annihilation, the root receives exactly one apple at second `d` iff the number of tree nodes at depth `d` is odd. Therefore the required total is simply the number of depths whose node count parity is 1. Because parents satisfy `p_i < i`, depths can be computed in one forward pass. The program toggles parity for each node depth and prints the sum of odd-depth parities.

Complexity: O(n) time, O(n) memory. Input contract: first line `n`, followed by `n-1` parent indices. Output contract: one integer answer on stdout. Suggested validation properties: sample agreement, stars/chains/random trees, and parity equivalence against a slower time-step simulation on small instances.
